curriculum.title: Grade 5
curriculum.description: Ontario mathematics curriculum for YRDSB learners. Every expectation has a practice or guided activity. Activities illustrate the expectation; they are not a certification of mastery.

children.title: Social-emotional learning skills and the mathematical processes
children.description: These skills are integrated across the other strands, rather than taught only as a separate calculation unit.

children.title: Social-emotional learning skills and the mathematical processes
Manage emotions
children.description: Identify and manage emotions while engaging in mathematics.
children.example: Explain how you feel when a problem is unfamiliar.

children.title: Cope with challenges
children.description: Recognize stress and use strategies for coping with mathematical challenges.
children.example: Pause, try a drawing, or ask a useful question when stuck.

children.title: Persist and stay motivated
children.description: Maintain motivation and perseverance when working through problems.
children.example: Try another strategy after a first attempt does not work.

children.title: Collaborate and communicate
children.description: Build relationships, listen to different mathematical ideas, and communicate respectfully.
children.example: Compare two solution methods with a partner.

children.title: Confidence and self-awareness
children.description: Develop awareness of yourself as a capable mathematics learner.
children.example: Describe a strategy you have improved at using.

children.title: Critical and creative thinking
children.description: Think critically and creatively to support mathematical decisions and problem solving.
children.example: Explain whether an answer is reasonable and find another approach.

children.title: Number
children.description: Understand whole numbers, fractions, decimals, and percentages, then use operations to solve and check problems.

children.title: Whole numbers to 100,000
children.description: Read, represent, compose, and decompose whole numbers through 100,000 using place value and different tools.
children.example: Represent 48,306 as ten-thousands, thousands, hundreds, tens, and ones.

children.title: Compare and order whole numbers
children.description: Compare and order whole numbers through 100,000 in different contexts.

children.title: Equivalent fractions and mixed numbers
children.description: Represent equivalent fractions from halves through twelfths, including improper fractions and mixed numbers.
children.example: Show why 3/2 and 1½ represent the same amount.

children.title: Compare and order fractions
children.description: Compare and order fractions from halves through twelfths, including improper fractions and mixed numbers.
children.example: Which is greater: 3/4 or 5/6? Use a picture or number line.

children.title: Decimals through hundredths
children.description: Read, represent, compare, and order decimal numbers through hundredths.

children.title: Round decimals
children.description: Round decimal numbers to the nearest tenth.
children.example: Round 3.47 to the nearest tenth.

children.title: Fractions, decimals, and percentages
children.description: Explain equivalences among fractions, decimals through hundredths, and whole-number percentages using tools and drawings.
children.example: Represent one half as 0.50 and 50%.

children.title: Operation relationships and multi-step problems
children.description: Use operation properties and inverse relationships to solve whole-number and decimal problems requiring more than one operation, and check calculations.
children.example: Work out 2 + 3 × 4, explaining which operation comes first.

children.title: Multiplication and division facts
children.description: Recall multiplication facts through 12 × 12 and their related division facts.
children.example: Use 8 × 7 = 56 to explain 56 ÷ 8.

children.title: Mental math and estimation
children.description: Mentally multiply whole numbers by 0.1 and 0.01, and estimate sums and differences of decimals through hundredths.
children.example: Explain why 460 × 0.01 = 4.6.

children.title: Add and subtract whole numbers and decimals
children.description: Solve addition and subtraction problems with whole-number sums no greater than 100,000 and decimals through hundredths, using tools, strategies, and algorithms.
children.example: Calculate 24.75 − 8.60 and check by addition.

children.title: Add and subtract like-denominator fractions
children.description: Add and subtract fractions with matching denominators in different contexts. Unlike-denominator addition is an extension beyond this Grade 5 expectation.
children.example: Add 2/5 + 1/5 using fifths.

children.title: Two-digit multiplication
children.description: Multiply two-digit whole numbers by two-digit whole numbers using area models and algorithms, and connect the methods.
children.example: Calculate 24 × 13 using an area model.

children.title: Three-digit by two-digit division
children.description: Divide three-digit whole numbers by two-digit whole numbers using area models and algorithms; interpret any remainder appropriately.
children.example: Divide 156 ÷ 12 and explain the quotient.

children.title: Whole numbers and unit fractions
children.description: Multiply and divide one-digit whole numbers by unit fractions using tools and drawings.
children.example: Use fraction strips to explain 3 ÷ 1/2.

children.title: Equivalent ratios and rates
children.description: Represent and create equivalent ratios and rates using tools and models in different contexts.
children.example: If 2 notebooks cost $6, what would 4 notebooks cost at the same rate?

children.title: Algebra
children.description: Explore patterns, express relationships, solve equations and inequalities, and apply coding and mathematical modelling.

children.title: Recognize types of patterns
children.description: Identify and describe repeating, growing, and shrinking patterns, including patterns in real life.
children.example: Describe what happens in 30, 25, 20, 15, …

children.title: Represent patterns
children.description: Create and translate growing and shrinking patterns using different representations, including tables of values and graphs.
children.example: Show a growing tile pattern as a table and graph.

children.title: Rules, predictions, and missing elements
children.description: Find pattern rules, extend patterns, justify predictions, and identify missing elements in repeating, growing, and shrinking patterns.
children.example: Find the missing value in 4, 8, __, 16, 20.

children.title: Whole-number and decimal patterns
children.description: Create and describe patterns illustrating relationships among whole numbers, tenths, and hundredths.

children.title: Words, expressions, and pictures
children.description: Translate among words, algebraic expressions, and visual representations describing equivalent relationships.
children.example: Represent “three groups of a number plus two” with a drawing and an expression.

children.title: Evaluate expressions
children.description: Evaluate algebraic expressions involving whole numbers.
children.example: Find 3n + 2 when n = 4.

children.title: Solve and verify equations
children.description: Solve equations involving whole numbers through 100 in different contexts, and verify the solutions.
children.example: Solve x + 68 = 95 and substitute your answer to check.

children.title: Solve and graph inequalities
children.description: Solve inequalities involving one operation and whole numbers through 50, then verify and graph the solutions.
children.example: Find whole-number values satisfying x + 5 < 12.

children.title: Write mathematical code
children.description: Write and execute code representing mathematical situations, including conditional statements and other control structures.
children.example: Write an if/else rule that tells whether a whole number is even.

children.title: Read and modify code
children.description: Read and alter code with conditional statements and other control structures, and describe how changes affect outcomes.
children.example: Change a condition in a pattern program and explain the new output.

children.title: Model real-life situations
children.description: Understand a real-life problem, analyse assumptions, create a mathematical model, assess its results, and revise it. This overall expectation has no separate specific expectations.
children.example: Plan a seating arrangement, test the capacity, and revise the plan.

children.title: Data
children.description: Collect representative data, communicate it clearly, analyse it critically, and investigate probability.

children.title: Representative sampling
children.description: Explain why different sampling techniques matter when collecting a sample representative of a population.
children.example: Would surveying only a soccer team fairly represent the whole school?

children.title: Collect and organize data
children.description: Collect data about a population, using suitable sampling techniques, and organize it in relative-frequency tables.
children.example: Survey favourite activities and record each category as a fraction of the responses.

children.title: Choose and construct graphs
children.description: Select and justify appropriate graphs, including stacked-bar graphs, with suitable scales, sources, titles, and labels.
children.example: Compare two classes’ activity preferences with a stacked-bar graph.

children.title: Create infographics
children.description: Communicate a data story with an infographic using appropriate representations and relevant information.
children.example: Create an infographic about how students travel to school.

children.title: Mean, median, and mode
children.description: Determine the mean and median and identify any modes for whole-number and decimal data; explain what they reveal.
children.example: Find the mean, median, and mode of 2, 3, 3, 4, 8.

children.title: Interpret data and misleading graphs
children.description: Analyse data, including stacked-bar graphs and misleading graphs, ask questions, challenge assumptions, and justify conclusions.
children.example: Explain how a graph’s scale might exaggerate a difference.

children.title: Probabilities as fractions
children.description: Express event probabilities as fractions, place them on a probability line, and use them to make predictions.
children.example: What is the probability of rolling an even number on a fair six-sided die?

children.title: Theoretical and experimental probability
children.description: Determine and compare theoretical and experimental probabilities of an event.
children.example: Compare the expected chance of heads with results from 30 coin tosses.

children.title: Spatial sense
children.description: Reason about shapes, views, position, movement, and measurement.

children.title: Triangle properties and construction
children.description: Identify triangle properties and construct different types of triangles from given side lengths or angle measurements.
children.example: Construct a triangle with sides 5 cm, 6 cm, and 7 cm.

children.title: Congruent shapes
children.description: Identify and construct congruent triangles, rectangles, and parallelograms.
children.example: Decide whether two triangles have the same shape and size.

children.title: Top, front, and side views
children.description: Draw top, front, and side views of objects and match drawings to objects.
children.example: Draw three views of a structure made from cubes.

children.title: First-quadrant coordinates
children.description: Read and plot first-quadrant coordinates using various scales, and describe translations between points.
children.example: Plot (2, 4), then move it three units right.

children.title: Translations, reflections, and rotations
children.description: Perform translations, reflections, and rotations through 180° on a grid, and predict the results.
children.example: Rotate a triangle 90° about a marked point.

children.title: Metric estimation and measurement
children.description: Estimate and measure length, area, mass, and capacity using appropriate metric units.
children.example: Choose suitable units for a classroom’s area and a bottle’s capacity.

children.title: Convert larger metric units to smaller units
children.description: Use base-ten relationships to convert larger metric units into smaller ones.
children.example: Convert 2.5 m into centimetres.

children.title: Compare angles
children.description: Compare angles by matching them and measuring with appropriate non-standard units.
children.example: Compare two angles using the same paper angle wedge.

children.title: Measure and construct angles
children.description: Explain how protractors work; measure and construct angles through 180°; estimate using benchmark angles.
children.example: Use a protractor to construct a 65° angle.

children.title: Triangle and parallelogram areas
children.description: Use relationships among rectangles, parallelograms, and triangles to develop area formulas and solve problems.
children.example: Find the area of a triangle with base 8 cm and perpendicular height 5 cm.

children.title: Equal areas, different perimeters
children.description: Show that shapes with equal areas can have different perimeters, and solve related problems.
children.example: Compare the perimeters of 3 × 4 and 2 × 6 rectangles.

children.title: Financial literacy
children.description: Use money concepts and calculations to make informed financial decisions.

children.title: Money transfers
children.description: Describe ways money is transferred among individuals, organizations, and businesses.
children.example: Compare a cheque with an electronic transfer.

children.title: Transactions and sales tax
children.description: Estimate and calculate transaction costs for items priced in dollars and cents, including sales tax.
children.example: Calculate the total for two purchases using a given tax rate.

children.title: Basic budgets
children.description: Design basic budgets for different earning and spending situations.
children.example: Plan how to allocate $40 between spending and saving.

children.title: Credit and debt
children.description: Explain credit and debt and describe how they affect financial decisions.
children.example: Explain how borrowing money changes what you can spend later.

children.title: Unit rates and best value
children.description: Calculate unit rates for goods and services and identify which options offer better value.
children.example: Compare 5 apples for $1 with 3 apples for $0.75.

children.title: Taxes and public services
children.description: Describe taxes collected by different Canadian government levels and how revenue funds community services.
children.example: Connect examples of taxes to public services.

suggestedSequence: Place value, comparison, multiplication and division facts.
Operation properties, algorithms, and inverse checks.
Equivalent forms, comparisons, and Grade 5 operations.
Fractions, decimals, percentages, and equivalent ratios.
Shapes, coordinates, transformations, units, and area.
Data, probability, budgets, transactions, and value.
